interface.name: mx_shell_surface_manager_v1

description.summary: give shell roles and visibility to layer surfaces

interface.description:
This interface lets a shell give its zwlr_layer_surface_v1 surfaces shell state: a role, which says what the surface is for, and whether it is hidden. Layer shell alone orders surfaces only by layer; a role places a surface among the shell's other surfaces and the apps, and for some roles changes how input reaches it. Everything else about the surface (anchors, size, exclusive zone, keyboard interactivity) stays as layer shell defines it, except while it is hidden.
A role takes effect only while the surface is on the overlay layer. On any other layer it has no effect, and the surface stacks as layer shell defines. Hiding works on every layer, with or without a role.
While in effect, surfaces stack front to back by role, in this order:
1. prompt 2. edge 3. bar 4. osd 5. panel 6. osk 7. view 8. overlay-layer surfaces without a role 9. a fullscreen toplevel and its dialogs 10. top-layer surfaces 11. other toplevels, then the bottom and background layers
The one exception is osk: while a prompt surface has keyboard focus, osk stacks above prompts instead, so the prompt can be typed into. Several surfaces with one role stack among themselves newest first.
The compositor may offer this interface to privileged clients only. It may also give a layer surface without a role one by its own means, on the top layer as well as the overlay layer, such as treating the namespace "osk" as the osk role. It gives none the osk role this way while some surface has that role through this interface, hidden or not.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the layer surface already has a shell surface

entry.name: already_configured
entry.summary: the layer surface was already configured

enum.name: role
enum.description: What a layer surface is for. Each role's description says where it stacks and how input reaches it; see the interface description for the whole order.

entry.name: none
entry.description: The surface stacks and takes input as layer shell defines. For a surface that needs only the other shell state, such as hiding.

entry.name: view
entry.description: A screen of the shell that covers the apps, such as a home screen or an app switcher. It stacks above every toplevel, a fullscreen one included, and below every other role. Input reaches it as layer shell defines.

entry.name: osk
entry.description: An on-screen keyboard. It stacks above views and below panels, except while a prompt surface has keyboard focus: then it stacks above prompts, so the prompt can be typed into.

entry.name: osd
entry.description: Short-lived feedback such as a volume or brightness indicator. It stacks above panels, the keyboard and views, below bars.

entry.name: bar
entry.description: Persistent shell chrome such as a status bar, usually with an exclusive zone. It stacks above OSDs, below edge regions.

entry.name: edge
entry.description:
An input-only region along one edge of the output, for swipes in from that edge. The edge is the one the surface's anchors span: the surface is anchored to it, and to both edges beside it or to neither. Swipes away from that edge, towards the middle, are inward.
Edge regions stack above bars, below prompts. The compositor need not draw them, so their content may never be shown: it still sends frame callbacks, and answers wp_presentation feedback as discarded.
Pointer input passes through to what is beneath. A touch that begins on the region is held until the compositor decides whose it is. An inward swipe gives the whole touch sequence, from its start, to the region. Any other movement, the touch ending, another touch point, or the touch staying still for a short time gives it to what is beneath. Distances and times are compositor policy.

entry.name: prompt
entry.description: A question from the system that the user must answer, such as a power menu or a password dialog. It stacks above every other role, except the keyboard while a prompt has keyboard focus.

entry.name: panel
entry.description: A shell surface that slides over whatever is shown, such as quick settings or a notification shade. It stacks above the keyboard, views and every toplevel, and below OSDs, bars, edge regions and prompts, so the status bar stays in view over it. Input reaches it as layer shell defines.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager object. Shell surfaces already created from it remain valid.

request.name: get_shell_surface

description.summary: extend a layer surface with shell state

request.description:
Create an add-on object for a zwlr_layer_surface_v1 that gives it a role and lets it be hidden.
It must be made before the initial wl_surface.commit that precedes the first zwlr_layer_surface_v1.configure event; after that it raises already_configured. A layer surface has at most one shell surface at a time; a second raises already_constructed. A role value this version does not define raises invalid_role.
The role applies from the layer surface's next commit, and cannot change while the shell surface exists.

interface.name: mx_shell_surface_v1
interface.description: The role and visibility of one zwlr_layer_surface_v1. If the layer surface is destroyed, the shell surface becomes inert: its requests do nothing, and the client should destroy it.

request.name: set_hidden
request.description:
Hide (non-zero) or show (zero) the surface. Double-buffered: it applies on the next wl_surface.commit, with the rest of that commit, such as a new buffer.
While hidden, the surface is not shown. It receives no pointer, touch or keyboard input and cannot have keyboard focus. Its exclusive zone is ignored: other surfaces and toplevels are placed as if it had none. Frame callbacks requested while hidden are not done until the surface is shown and a frame of it has been displayed.
The surface keeps its buffer, role, layer, exclusive zone and other layer surface state, and still receives configure events. All of it takes effect again from the commit that shows it.
A surface starts shown, and may be hidden before its first buffer.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the shell surface. From the layer surface's next commit, it is shown and has no role, and stacks as layer shell defines. A new shell surface may be created for it only before its first configure, as for the first.
